Hi Samir / Aisha,

Thanks — quick technical write-up below. TL;DR: we support both removal and pseudonymization; customer-managed KMS for keying the hash is possible with an added key-wrapping step.

Options to consider (trade-offs):
1) Full removal at ingestion
   - No trace IDs stored, simplest for compliance but you lose cross-request correlation.
2) Pseudonymization (hash + salt)
   - We can compute H = HMAC_SHA256(salt, trace_id) at ingestion. If FinBank wants KMS-managed salt, we store the salt encrypted and use a transient unwrapped key during processing; hashes are stored in the same log index by default but can be routed to a redacted index on request.
3) Tokenization service (lookup table)
   - We generate tokens and store mapping in a customer-only encrypted store; requires additional reads for correlation.

Header scrubbing: we have configurable rules (regex or explicit header list). On your list (x-cust-id, x-user-email, x-session-token, x-partner-id) we can apply either removal or pseudonymization. For x-user-email we recommend deterministic hashing + canonicalization (lowercase + trim) to reduce collisions.

Retention & residency: logs can be retained 30 days in eu-west-1 via a dedicated bucket + lifecycle. We can export an immutable audit snapshot for compliance on request.

Access control: RBAC mapping is possible; we'll mirror your SSO groups to Redwood roles via SCIM if you want automated sync.

Open items for FinBank:
- Confirm desired mode for trace IDs (remove / pseudonymize / token).
- Confirm which headers to treat as PII vs telemetry.
- Confirm whether hashed trace IDs should live in the same index (easier for ops) or a separate redacted index (better separation).

I'll put a short tech appendix into the shared drive and a sample config file.
